rules.route: Residence permit as an artist, musician or performer (UDI)

others.route: Residence permit as an artist, musician or performer (UDI)

note: Norway: EEA and Swiss nationals live and work freely (the eea list). Everyone else needs a residence permit from UDI as an artist, musician or performer; performers and their support staff need none for concerts or performances totalling at most 14 days in a calendar year (taken as 14 in 365), and British musicians and artists with no employer in Norway none for up to 90 days in 180, the police notified in writing beforehand.

sources.title: UDI (Norwegian Directorate of Immigration), Want to apply: Exchange programmes, culture and organisational work
sources.said: You can be granted a residence permit in Norway if you are going on a working holiday for young adults, if you are a working guest in agriculture, an employee of a humanitarian/non-profit/religious organisation, or an artist, musician or performer. ... Performers, artists, musicians and their support staff do not need a residence permit if they are to have concerts or performances in Norway for a total of maximum 14 days during a calendar year. You or your client must notify the police in writing before you enter Norway. ... British musicians, artists and their support staff who do not have an employer in Norway do not need a residence permit if they are going to perform, participate in competitions or hold rehearsals in Norway for up to 90 days in a 180-day period.
